EDITION Europe Germany preparing sweeping ban on Chinese mobile network equipment: Report Planned security classification of 5G base stations could effectively exclude Huawei, ZTE from country's telecommunications networks Oliver Towfigh Nia 04 November 2026 • Update : 04 November 2026 BERLIN Germany is preparing a sweeping ban on Chinese-made equipment in its mobile networks over security concerns, potentially excluding suppliers such as Huawei and ZTE, business daily Handelsblatt reported Wednesday.
An Interior Ministry spokesperson told the newspaper that a "turning point in security policy" required a "comprehensive, forward-looking, and re-evaluated approach to dependencies and risks concerning critical infrastructure."
The move follows plans by the Federal Network Agency to classify 5G base stations as highly sensitive components for the first time.
The stations connect smartphones to mobile networks and form a key part of Germany's telecommunications infrastructure.
Because equipment manufacturers typically supply integrated systems whose components are not always interchangeable, a ban on Chinese-made base stations could effectively exclude Huawei and ZTE from the market.
Alternative suppliers include European companies Nokia and Ericsson, as well as South Korea's Samsung.
The Interior Ministry also emphasized the importance of reducing security risks as Germany develops its next-generation 6G network, saying the priority was "to avoid the use of critical components from potentially untrustworthy manufacturers."
It welcomed the continued development of telecommunications security requirements to address emerging technologies and evolving threats.
